objects.description: Boolean-like type used by DALI C API to ensure a stable, 1-byte storage across C and C++. In C++, it aliases bool if bool is 1 byte; otherwise it aliases uint8_t. In C, it is typedef’d to uint8_t. Use for cross-language ABI-safe boolean values; treat any non-zero as true when interoperating with C.

objects.definition:
typedef enum _DALIDataType {
  DALI_NO_TYPE           = -1,
  DALI_UINT8             =  0,
  DALI_UINT16            =  1,
  DALI_UINT32            =  2,
  DALI_UINT64            =  3,
  DALI_INT8              =  4,
  DALI_INT16             =  5,
  DALI_INT32             =  6,
  DALI_INT64             =  7,
  DALI_FLOAT16           =  8,
  DALI_FLOAT             =  9,
  DALI_FLOAT64           = 10,
  DALI_BOOL              = 11,
  DALI_STRING            = 12,
  DALI_BOOL_VEC          = 13,
  DALI_INT_VEC           = 14,
  DALI_STRING_VEC        = 15,
  DALI_FLOAT_VEC         = 16,
  DALI_TF_FEATURE        = 17,
  DALI_TF_FEATURE_VEC    = 18,
  DALI_TF_FEATURE_DICT   = 19,
  DALI_IMAGE_TYPE        = 20,
  DALI_DATA_TYPE         = 21,
  DALI_INTERP_TYPE       = 22,
  DALI_TENSOR_LAYOUT     = 23,
  DALI_PYTHON_OBJECT     = 24,
  DALI_TENSOR_LAYOUT_VEC = 25,
  DALI_DATA_TYPE_VEC     = 26,
  DALI_NUM_BUILTIN_TYPES,
  DALI_CUSTOM_TYPE_START = 1001,
  DALI_DATA_TYPE_FORCE_INT32 = 0x7fffffff
} daliDataType_t;
objects.description: C-compatible enumeration of DALI’s type identifiers used for pipeline I/O, serialization, and runtime type queries. Values are ABI-stable; do not reorder or change existing numeric assignments. Includes built-in integral, floating point, string, vector-of-primitive markers, and several framework-specific or enum-type markers. DALI_CUSTOM_TYPE_START reserves range for user-defined extensions. FORCE_INT32 ensures 32-bit enum size.

functions.name: daliDataTypeName
functions.description: Returns a human-readable display name for a DALI built-in data type. If the type is not one of the recognized built-in values, the function returns NULL. Typical usage: pass a daliDataType_t and use the returned string for logging, error messages, or UI display; check for NULL to handle unknown/custom types.
requirements: Argument t must be a value of daliDataType_t (may be any value, including custom/unknown).
Caller must check for a NULL return to handle unknown/unrecognized types.
The returned pointer refers to a static string literal; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: daliDataTypeIsFloatingPoint
functions.description: Returns true if type is a floating-point DALI data type (float16, float32, or float64); false otherwise. Intended for quickly classifying element types.
requirements: Argument type must be a value of daliDataType_t (any value allowed).
Pure, side-effect free; safe to call in any context, including constexpr in C++.

functions.name: daliDataTypeIsIntegral
functions.description: Returns true if type is an integral DALI data type (bool or signed/unsigned integers); false otherwise. Useful for dispatching integer-specific code paths.
requirements: Argument type must be a value of daliDataType_t (any value allowed).
Pure, side-effect free; safe to call in any context, including constexpr in C++.

functions.name: daliDataTypeIsSigned
functions.description: Returns true if type is a signed DALI data type, including floating-point and signed integer types; false otherwise.
requirements: Argument type must be a value of daliDataType_t (any value allowed).
Pure, side-effect free; safe to call in any context, including constexpr in C++.

functions.name: daliDataTypeIsUnsigned
functions.description: Returns true if type is an unsigned integer DALI data type (including bool); false otherwise.
requirements: Argument type must be a value of daliDataType_t (any value allowed).
Pure, side-effect free; safe to call in any context, including constexpr in C++.

functions.name: daliDataTypeIsEnum
functions.description: Returns true if type denotes an enumerated metadata-like DALI type (DALI_DATA_TYPE, DALI_IMAGE_TYPE, or DALI_INTERP_TYPE); false otherwise.
requirements: Argument type must be a value of daliDataType_t (any value allowed).
Pure, side-effect free; safe to call in any context, including constexpr in C++.
